2608.19907.title: Spike-based Belief Propagation in Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
2608.19907.paper_summary: This paper presents a Bayesian control framework that integrates spike-based dynamics with probabilistic inference for adaptive control. Bayesian inference is widely regarded as a core computational principle of brain function, providing a normative framework for perception, decision-making, and learning under uncertainty. By combining a biologically inspired spiking neural model with Bayesian inference principles, we propose a brain-like control algorithm capable of operating in uncertain environments. We use the mountain car parking problem as a benchmark with non-linear dynamics. Our results demonstrate that the proposed controller can successfully update states in real time and generate goal-directed action plans through spike-driven dynamics. The results highlight the proposed model's potential as a bridge between computational neuroscience and probabilistic control theory.
2608.19907.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文提出了一個貝葉斯控制框架，將基於脈衝的動態與適應性控制的概率推斷相結合。貝葉斯推斷被廣泛認為是大腦功能的核心計算原則，為在不確定性下的感知、決策和學習提供了一個規範框架。通過將生物啟發的脈衝神經模型與貝葉斯推斷原則相結合，我們提出了一種類似大腦的控制算法，能夠在不確定的環境中運作。我們使用山地車停車問題作為具有非線性動態的基準。我們的結果表明，所提出的控制器可以成功地實時更新狀態，並通過脈衝驅動的動態生成以目標為導向的行動計劃。結果突顯了所提出模型作為計算神經科學與概率控制理論之間橋樑的潛力。
